title: PTPv2: dissect management TLVs
description:
Implement todo and missing PTPv2 management TLVs.

I tested with [ptp.pcapng](/uploads/d6e5d77ec8d2266a04b3b6babad3d8a0/ptp.pcapng)

I build the packets with the [libptpmgmt](https://gitlab.com/erezgeva/libptpmgmt) library.

notes.body:
added 1 commit
  • 4f6f1fe9 - Dissect PTPv2 management TLVs
[Compare with previous version](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/19728/diffs?diff_id=1343884196&start_sha=f430302c97ce99f142214c119b0bfaf5fbcdb06d)
This assumes N is always even, which it may not be, especially when you have malformed messages!

Yes,
The address are always even.  
Ethernet use 6 octets (or 8 for EUI-64).  
IPv4 use 4 octets.  
IPv6 use 16 octets (128 bits).  
DeviceNet (CAN) use 2 octets.  
ControlNet use 2 octets.  
PROFINET (Ethernet) use 6 octets.

As all other fields are fixed size.
I can safely say that this TLV always sum to even size!

You can safely say that this TLV *should* always sum to even size. But that doesn't account for rainy-day scenarios, in which the packet is malformed. `N` is read straight from the packet data, so there is *no* guarantee that this value is even.

Remember, Wireshark is pulled out whenever there are problem, not only when the protocol is properly working. So you must account for packet data being bad. Heck, we even make it bad in fuzz-test CI pipelines.

@JaapKeuter  
How about adding a warning if `hf_ptp_v2_mm_protocolAddress_length` is even?  
And a warning if `offset` is odd?  
I am new to this code, can you please link an example?

@JaapKeuter, @johnthacker  
Does adding `DISSECTOR_ASSERT_HINT` for these condition covers?
No, `DISSECTOR_ASSERT` is for problems in the dissector logic itself. For unexpected malformed packet data, expert info items are used.

@johnthacker   
Can you link an example please?
Replace with `expert_add_info()`
This assumes N is always even, which it may not be, especially when you have malformed messages!

Yes, same logic as above.  
<del>
Would not malformed need to be handled in a different way?  
I prefer to see an error if the packet is malformed, rather than add a pad when it should not be there.  
PTP say message need to be even, pad are added on this base only!
block
</del>

> I prefer to see an error if the packet is malformed,

If you want to always treat it as an error if N is not even, then you should add an informative error to the `hf_ptp_v2_mm_protocolAddress_length` and stop processing there, rather than mysteriously fail later.

It's also bad to add two items for the same field with the same offset, `hf_ptp_v2_mm_protocolAddress`. That will confuse people using the filter language because the counts will be off. Also retrieving data later in the frame before adding earlier fields is confusing. This is a case for using a different field (FT_NONE or the somewhat deprecated text-only node.)
Ideally, I would add an FT_NONE containing the fixed portion and then set the correct length later after retrieving N, so that one can proceed through the packet monotonically.

Sure we can add a test for `hf_ptp_v2_mm_protocolAddress_length` to ensure it is even.  
@johnthacker, I am now to this code, can you please link an example? 

Split `hf_ptp_v2_mm_protocolAddress` to two indexes make sense.  
However I leave the address value, as this is what this structure is all about.  
Users want to see the address before they open the subtree!  
I skip the `FT_NONE` in this case.

Add `hf_ptp_v2_mm_protocolAddressStruct` index and left `hf_ptp_v2_mm_protocolAddress` inside.  
Though I skip `FT_NONE` and left the address on `hf_ptp_v2_mm_protocolAddressStruct`.
